title: Notched hydroid cups and annulated stems are both due to surface tension

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Notched hydroid cups and annulated stems are both due to surface tension

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The notching of the rim of hydroid calycles and the annular constrictions of their cylindrical stems are phenomena of the same order, both produced by surface tension acting on the structures while they are still fluid or semifluid films, as in the beaded rim of a splash.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In the case of the hydroid calycle (Fig. 72), we are led to the conclusion that the two common and conspicuous features of notching or indentation of the cup, and of constriction or annulation of the long cylindrical stem, are phenomena of the same order and are due to surface-tension in both cases alike.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Splashes and hydroid calycles”. Scope: calycles and stems of campanularian hydroids and other small organic cups

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-13: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A shared instability model could yield discriminating geometric and perturbational predictions. Existing specimens mainly record endpoints and are inadequate to establish surface tension as the cause during formation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Image hydroid calycle rims and stems during secretion, quantify notch and annulation wavelengths, and test whether one surface-tension instability model predicts both geometries and their response to tension perturbation. Distinct developmental patterning or formation after solidification would refute the shared mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Developmental time series and tension perturbations are scarce.

The common-cause model lacks a specified parameterization.

Final museum morphology does not reveal whether tissue was fluid during patterning.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Museum images make a geometric comparison of rim notches and stem rings possible for campanularian hydroids. That comparison is only a proxy for a shared surface-tension cause, because the same regularity can be produced by periodic growth. The fluid or semifluid stage Thompson invokes is not in the specimens, which are already solidified.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure notch spacing on hydroid calycle rims and annulation spacing on their stems, and test whether both match the wavelength of a surface-tension instability on a fluid rim or cylinder of that radius. A shared match to that wavelength would support one surface-tension cause; spacings set by polyp size or genetic segmentation, independent of radius, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Specimen portals provide images and occurrences, not notch measurements.

Growth pulses and patterned perisarc secretion can mimic splash-like spacing.

The structures are fossilised as rigid perisarc, so the fluid stage is not observed.
